open_points.subject: ProofResult identity and recomputation
open_points.text: “Substitution: proving the same version gives the same result.”; “the proof refuses a binding that is not `accepted`”; “whether a flow version whose proof failed because a binding was not yet accepted can be proven again later — closed by A05 (yes).”
open_points.question: When mutable dependencies such as binding acceptance change, is the later proof a different ProofResult, and what facts distinguish it from the earlier result?
options: ProofResult identity includes the relevant dependency state
Each proof invocation is a separately identified observation
The first result remains authoritative for that flow version
open_points.default_guess: Treat each computed result as a value of the flow version plus the dependency state observed during that proof.

open_points.subject: Run failure while another branch waits
open_points.text: “No wait ends by itself”; “The run is `failed` when no node can run any more and some node failed”; “While some nodes wait, independent branches keep running.”
open_points.question: If one branch has failed and all remaining unfinished branches are waiting for approval, service recovery, or outcome resolution, does the run remain waiting or end `failed`?
options: Remain `awaiting_approval` or `pending` until every wait is explicitly resolved
End `failed` immediately and discard the remaining waits
Use different precedence depending on the waiting reason
open_points.default_guess: Keep the run waiting because an existing wait may end only through its specified owner or resume action; determine `failed` after those waits are resolved.

open_points.subject: Cancellation or refusal with concurrent work
open_points.text: “the run ends `cancelled`; nothing further is sent”; “When the owner refuses an effect, the run ends `refused`”; “a file moves between nodes through a spool that belongs to its run and is emptied when the run ends”
open_points.question: What happens to other branches that are already executing or have an effect in flight when the run is cancelled or becomes `refused`, and when may their records and spool bytes be finalized?
options: Finish or classify already-started work before making the run final
Make the run final immediately but continue recording late outcomes and retain required spool bytes
Abort work immediately and map every interrupted execution or effect to specified terminal records
open_points.default_guess: Stop scheduling and sending immediately, allow already-started work to reach a recorded terminal or unknown outcome, and only then finalize the run and remove its spool.

open_points.subject: Service response that echoes a secret
open_points.text: “A service's own answer that echoes one verbatim is withheld”; “the kernel never puts one into a function, a flow, a trace or an answer.”
open_points.question: When a validated service response contains a configured secret verbatim, what model records and lifecycle outcome are created for the operation node and run?
options: Fail the node without creating an output value
Create only a digest-and-class placeholder and continue
Remove the secret-bearing portion and validate the remainder
Keep the value internally but withhold it only from readers
open_points.default_guess: Fail the operation node, create no StoredValue or SpooledFile containing the secret, and retain only bounded non-secret failure facts.
